must_cover: Inventory of ALL Agent(subagent_type=...) spawn sites that emit sprint-task work (use grep output already gathered by PO — see § identified_spawn_sites below)
Model 1 dispatcher-wrap design: caller holds claim around spawn, releases after spawn returns OR if spawn fails. TTL ≤ sprint-task TTL (3600s).

Same task_id pattern: outer claim MUST use `task:<task_id>` matching the agent's self-claim (Model 2) — current_holder check then resolves second claim as idempotent same-session OR cross-session collision SKIP

Decision: for sprint-task kind, does the agent self-claim become a no-op (idempotent owner match) OR is it removed entirely? Architect picks one and justifies. PM scopes; agent-father implements per architect.

Owner-agent identity rule: outer claim owner_agent = dispatcher identity (e.g. `dev-team-router` or the dispatcher's parent agent name) NOT the spawned agent. Inner self-claim (if kept) keeps original owner_agent (e.g. `developer`, `qa`). This permits same-task_id chain without false collision.
Failure modes: spawn returns error → outer dispatcher releases lock immediately, allowing peer to retry. Spawn hangs → TTL expiry (3600s) is fallback.
DO NOT retroactively claim in-flight agents (race risk per dev-team flag c221).
Migration order: pure dispatcher .md edits (no code, no MCP changes); agent-side self-claim stays AS-IS during rollout; remove or no-op self-claim ONLY after one full cycle observation.
